subject: [Action required] Route Experiments: metrics cardinality risk + tagging restrictions (SRE review before broader beta)
body:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 24, 2025 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: [Action required] Route Experiments: metrics cardinality risk + tagging restrictions (SRE review before broader beta)

Team,

Before we enable Route Experiments for the next beta tranche, I want to flag a high-risk issue: experiment dimensions on high-volume metrics can explode cardinality (and cost), and can destabilize the metrics pipeline.

What changed / what’s coming:
- We’re adding experiment attribution dimensions (experiment_id, variant_id) into OTel spans and some metrics (ref: ENG-9026 / PR-28489).
- We also want route-level breakdowns in Console (route + experiment + variant), which makes it tempting to tag everything.

SRE position: we need a tagging policy and an explicit SRE review gate before broader beta.

Proposed restrictions (initial):
1) Do NOT tag experiment_id/variant_id on all request metrics by default.
   - Allowed: a small set of pre-approved RED metrics (request_count, error_count, request_latency) and ONLY where we can cap label sets.
   - Not allowed: token-level metrics and per-model/per-route high-card combos with experiment_id.

2) Route identifier MUST be normalized.
   - No raw paths.
   - Use route_id (stable ID) or route_template (sanitized template) only.

3) Cap the possible label sets:
   - Max active experiments per route (hard validation in control plane).
   - Max variants per experiment.
   - TTL / expiration required.

4) Traces/logs can carry rich attribution, but metrics need guardrails.
   - OK to put experiment_id/variant_id on spans (sampling + rate limiting). Metrics must be stricter.

Asks:
- Logan: can you propose a concrete “allowed tags by signal” table (metrics vs traces vs logs) so we can sign off?
- Allison: can you sanity check this against existing observability standards (naming + label policy) and any prior incidents?
- Sean: if you agree, I’d like to treat this as an explicit SRE gate: we don’t expand beta enablement until we have (a) tagging restrictions merged, (b) dashboards for cardinality/attribution health, (c) rollback plan.

Attachments:
- route-experiments-metrics-tagging-proposal-v2.pdf
- cardinality-budget-estimate-2025-02-24.xlsx

Thanks,
Priya
—
Priya Natarajan
SRE / Observability
Redwood Inference


----

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 24, 2025 at 10:03 AM PT
Subject: Re: [Action required] Route Experiments: metrics cardinality risk + tagging restrictions (SRE review before broader beta)

Agree this is a real footgun.

Concrete proposal (v0) for where experiment attribution is allowed:

A) Metrics (Prom/OTel)
- Allowed to add experiment_id + variant_id:
  1) redwood.router.request_count
  2) redwood.router.request_error_count
  3) redwood.router.request_latency_ms (histogram)

- Conditions:
  - route_id must be the stable canonical route identifier (not raw path)
  - no model_id on those same series when experiment_id is present (we can still do model-level without experiment attribution)
  - region is OK (bounded), customer/account is NOT OK

- Not allowed (for now):
  - token counters (input_tokens, output_tokens) with experiment_id. Too high volume + hard to reason about label budgets.
  - per-kernel/per-batch runtime metrics with experiment_id (way too spiky/high-card).

B) Traces (OTel spans)
- Put experiment_id + variant_id on request root span + routing decision span.
- Sampling: keep current head-based sampling; add tail-based sampling rule for “guardrail triggered” traces.

C) Logs
- Add attribution to router access logs (structured): experiment_id, variant_id, route_id, config_version.

On caps/validation:
- We can add server-side validation to enforce:
  - max_variants <= 5
  - required end_time (or max_duration_days)
  - one active experiment per route (unless we introduce explicit priority later)

We should also add a “label cardinality watch” dashboard/alert (maybe per-metric time series count + top label sets) before beta expansion.

If this works, I’ll update ENG-9026 acceptance criteria and coordinate with Caleb on the ingestion side.

Logan


----

From: Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 24, 2025 at 11:19 AM PT
Subject: Re: [Action required] Route Experiments: metrics cardinality risk + tagging restrictions (SRE review before broader beta)

+1 to Logan’s table; a few notes from the observability standards side:

1) Naming / dimensions consistency
- Please keep the attribute names aligned with ADR-048 (experiment_id, variant_id, route_id, region).
- Avoid introducing both route_template and route_id in parallel on metrics. Pick route_id as canonical on metrics; templates can live in analytics tables.

2) Hard “no” list
- customer_id / api_key / user_id must never be metric labels.
- Any free-form header values (including stickiness key) must not be labels.

3) Route normalization
- I recommend we treat “route_id required” as a router contract (if missing, tag as route_id=unknown and increment a separate counter).

4) Rollups as the escape hatch
- For Console “quality/cost per variant”, we should rely on analytics rollups keyed by (route_id, experiment_id, variant_id, region) rather than trying to put everything into metrics labels.

If you want, I can put together a one-pager to include in the beta readiness checklist (“Cardinality policy for Route Experiments”).

Allison


----

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 24, 2025 at 12:07 PM PT
Subject: Re: [Action required] Route Experiments: metrics cardinality risk + tagging restrictions (SRE review before broader beta)

Approved in principle, with conditions.

Gate for broader beta enablement:
1) Merge tagging restrictions (as described: bounded set of router metrics only; no model_id + experiment_id combo; no token metrics with experiment labels).
2) Add a dashboard that lets on-call see:
   - total time series count for the affected metrics
   - top N label sets by cardinality
   - ingestion drops / backpressure indicators
3) Feature flag must be the brake:
   - If we see pipeline issues, we need to be able to disable experiment metric labels quickly without disabling the whole product.

Please also document “what we will not support in beta” so Support isn’t surprised (e.g., “no per-model metrics by variant in near real time”).

Marissa — FYI this is non-negotiable for stability.

Sean


----

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 24, 2025 at 2:37 PM PT
Subject: Re: [Action required] Route Experiments: metrics cardinality risk + tagging restrictions (SRE review before broader beta)

Thanks all. Capturing decisions + next steps:

Decisions (beta):
- Metrics: experiment_id/variant_id labels allowed ONLY on 3 router RED metrics (count, error_count, latency histogram) with route_id + region.
- Disallowed: token-level metrics with experiment attribution; any customer/user identifiers; model_id combined with experiment labels.
- Traces/logs: OK to include experiment_id/variant_id on request spans and structured access logs (sampling applies).
- Control plane validation: enforce caps (max variants, required end time) and block multiple active experiments per route (until we design priority semantics).

Action items:
- Logan: update ENG-9026 + coordinate PR updates; add explicit “no model_id + experiment_id” check in code path.
- Allison: please draft the one-pager for the beta readiness checklist + attribute naming guidance.
- Priya/Sean: we’ll add SRE sign-off as a checkbox in the beta expansion plan.
- Marissa: please ensure the Console requirements reflect that deep per-model variant breakdowns come from analytics rollups, not real-time metrics.

Once (1) restrictions are merged and (2) the cardinality dashboard exists, we can proceed with broader beta enablement.

Priya
